findings.claim: The new cache-hit fast path skips the Content-Type handling done by bufferToFormData(arrayBuffer, headers.get('Content-Type') || ''), so parseBody can now succeed (or return different data) for requests whose Content-Type the slow path would have rejected.
findings.rationale: Previously every call went through bufferToFormData with the request's Content-Type, which branches on multipart vs urlencoded and throws for unsupported/malformed types. With a pre-populated bodyCache.formData (set by a prior c.req.formData() call or middleware) that validation is bypassed. Medium confidence this is an intended trade-off, but it is a visible behavior change for existing callers.

findings.claim: A cached bodyCache.formData that is a rejecting promise is awaited here with no try/catch, so parseBody now re-throws that cached parse error, and awaiting a shared promise can leave an unhandled rejection path.
findings.rationale: bodyCache.formData may hold an in-flight Promise<FormData> stored by HonoRequest.formData() or by the tail of this same function; if parsing fails it rejects. Before this change parseBody produced its own error from arrayBuffer()/bufferToFormData. Moderate confidence; depends on how the cache is populated elsewhere.

findings.claim: The cast `await (request.bodyCache.formData as FormData | Promise<FormData>)` is an unchecked assertion; if bodyCache.formData holds anything other than a FormData/Promise<FormData> (e.g. a rejected placeholder or a non-FormData value set by user code), convertFormDataToBodyData will receive an unexpected shape instead of failing loudly.
findings.rationale: The truthiness check plus the cast performs no runtime validation. Low-to-medium confidence that this matters in practice, but the assertion hides a potential type mismatch that the previous code path could not hit.

findings.claim: On a cache hit the converted BodyData is not memoized and aliases values (e.g. File entries) from the shared cached FormData, so repeated parseBody calls re-do the conversion and callers can observe/mutate objects shared with c.req.formData().
findings.rationale: Minor efficiency and aliasing concern introduced by reusing the cached FormData instead of re-parsing a fresh buffer; low confidence this is problematic, but worth a second look if callers mutate the returned body data.
